mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with three consecutive months of declining FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 1.5% and rises by more than 0.1 percentage points over three months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the FEDFUNDS threshold, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and declines in the unemployment rate signal a tightening cycle with a strong labor market, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising > 0.1pp in 3 months and UNRATE falling > 0.1pp in 3 months
regime_hint: tightening cycle with strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE falling, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, declining housing starts (HOUST) and contracting retail sales (RSAFS) signal weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods with declining HOUST and RSAFS, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with three consecutive months of rising PAYEMS, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.5% and remains below this threshold, it signals a tight labor market that may trigger wage inflation and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with UNRATE < 3.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signal a broad-based economic slowdown in consumer demand and manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falling > 0.5% in 3 months and INDPRO falling > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with declining HOUST and INDPRO, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In post-shock recovery regimes, industrial production (INDPRO) rebounding above its 12-month moving average signals strengthening manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of post-shock recovery periods with INDPRO rebounding above 12-month MA, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
